instructions.heroTitle: How to run, edit and extend this theme
instructions.heroLead: This theme ships as source templates plus a zero-dependency build script. Pages are assembled from partials and section templates, and every piece of content comes from a JSON file that is also served at runtime.
instructions.stepsText: Four steps from a fresh checkout to a running site. Node 18 or newer is the only requirement — there are no packages to install.

steps.title: Install nothing
steps.text: The build script is a single ES module with zero dependencies. Confirm you have Node 18+: node --version.

steps.title: Build the site
steps.text: From the repository root run node theme/build.mjs. HTML pages are written to the output root, assets are copied, and a manifest is produced.

steps.title: Serve it locally
steps.text: Any static server works: npx serve . or python3 -m http.server 8080. Open the printed URL and browse.

steps.title: Watch while editing
steps.text: Run node theme/build.mjs --watch. Templates, sections, partials and data changes rebuild in well under a second.

instructions.treeText: Source of truth is the theme/ directory. Everything at the repository root is generated output — do not edit it by hand.

tree.v: Zero-dependency static site generator: front matter, tokens, includes, loops, conditionals, data derivation.
Site settings, generation rules for service / project / post detail pages, sitemap and robots options.
All content: site, services, projects, posts, process, testimonials, team, pricing, faq, offices, logos, stats.
Per-page section parameters. Front matter sets page: <id> and the matching object is merged into scope.
Chrome: head/body macros, icon sprite, header, mega menu drawer, footer, font declarations.
One template per section — every block in the library, reusable across pages with different parameters.
Hand-written page templates composed from section includes.
Detail templates looped over data by the generator (service, project, blog post).
Long-form article bodies, included into the blog post template.
Eight stylesheets: tokens, base, layout, components, sections, motion, utilities, responsive.
Seven modules: util, api, chrome, motion, sections, forms, theme. Vanilla, deferred, no dependencies.
Original AI-generated imagery referenced by data and page parameters.
Generated copy of the content files, served at runtime as the front-end JSON API.
Generated build report: page list, warnings, timings, asset inventory.

instructions.editText: Content edits never require touching a template. Change a JSON file, rebuild, and every page that reads it updates.

edits.k: Change the business name, phone, address or social links
Add, remove or rename a service
edits.v: theme/src/data/services.json — the detail page is generated automatically

edits.k: Add a project to the portfolio

edits.v: Add a post object in theme/src/data/posts.json and a body file in theme/src/content/posts/

edits.k: Change what a section says on one page
edits.v: theme/src/data/pages/<file>.json — find the page id and edit its parameters

edits.k: Change the palette, type scale or spacing rhythm
Change header, drawer or footer markup

instructions.apiText: Every content file is published under assets/data/ as a plain JSON endpoint. The browser layer reads them on load; you can read them from anything else.

instructions.apiNote: Responses are static files with no server logic, so they can be served from any host, CDN or object store. Set body[data-api] to a base URL to point the browser layer somewhere else.
instructions.motionText: All animation is vanilla JS plus CSS, gated behind html.js and disabled entirely under prefers-reduced-motion. Every effect is a data attribute you can add to any element.

motionItems.v: IntersectionObserver fade-and-rise, with optional data-reveal-delay in milliseconds.
Word-by-word text reveal for headings, staggered by word index.
Seamless scrolling band; data-speed controls seconds per loop.
Subtle scroll-linked offset; the value is the travel factor.
Pins one column of a two-column section while the other scrolls.
Slow scale-and-drift on hero and feature imagery.
Pointer attraction on buttons and links, released on mouseleave.
Perspective tilt on cards, bounded and eased back to neutral.
Counts a number up on first view; respects suffix, prefix and decimals.

instructions.motionNote: To turn motion off globally, set data-motion="off" on <html>. Reduced-motion users get the same content with transitions replaced by instant state changes.
instructions.ctaText: The product requirements document covers identity, typography, spacing, component contracts and the full section library.

style-guide.heroLead: The complete visual system: colour tokens, the type scale, spacing rhythm, buttons, cards, forms, navigation patterns and every section in the library — documented against live examples.
style-guide.paletteText: Five base colours plus four surface themes. Every component reads tokens, never literals, so a rebrand is a single file change.
style-guide.typeText: Two families plus a mono for eyebrows, meta and counters. Display uses an italic for emphasis words; body stays upright at 162% leading.
style-guide.spaceText: A four-pixel base with a fluid section rhythm. Container width caps at 1440px with 24px gutters, widening to 40px above 1200px.
style-guide.btnText: The signature control is a pill with a doubled label that slides on hover, plus a rotating arrow medallion. Four variants cover every context.
style-guide.compText: Class names are the public API of the theme. Sections expose a single .s-* root; everything inside is namespaced beneath it.

privacy.legalIntro: This notice explains what personal information Woodex Interior collects when you use this website or enquire about a project, why we collect it, how long we keep it, and the choices you have. It is written to be read, not skimmed past.

legalSections.title: Who we are
legalSections.body:
Woodex Interior is an interior design and fit-out practice trading from Studio 4, Gulberg Galleria, Main Boulevard, Gulberg III, Lahore 54660, Pakistan. For the purposes of this notice we are the controller of the personal information described below.

Questions about this notice, or about your information, should go to studio@woodexinterior.pk or +92 300 0000000.

legalSections.title: What we collect
legalSections.body:
Information you give us. When you submit an enquiry form, book a consultation or subscribe to the journal, you give us your name, email address, telephone number, the city your project is in, the type of project, an indicative area and budget, a target date, and anything you write in the message field — including any floor plans or photographs you attach.

Information collected automatically. Our server logs record the pages requested, the referring address, the browser and device type, and the time of the request. We use these logs to diagnose faults and to understand which pages are useful. If analytics are enabled they are configured without cross-site identifiers and without advertising use.

Information we do not collect. We do not collect payment card details on this website, we do not build advertising profiles, and we do not sell or rent personal information to anyone.

legalSections.title: Why we use it
legalSections.body:
• To respond to your enquiry and, where you ask, to prepare a proposal or budget range.
  • To schedule and run consultations, site visits and workshop visits.
  • To administer a live project: programmes, site access, approvals, deliveries and invoicing.
  • To send the monthly journal note, but only where you have subscribed and until you unsubscribe.
  • To keep the website secure, to diagnose faults and to understand aggregate usage.
  • To meet legal, tax and regulatory obligations that apply to a construction business in Pakistan.

legalSections.title: Lawful basis
legalSections.body: We process enquiry and project information because it is necessary to take steps at your request before entering a contract, and to perform that contract once signed. We process journal subscriptions on the basis of your consent, which you can withdraw at any time by unsubscribing. We process server logs and security information on the basis of our legitimate interest in operating a secure website. We process some information because we are legally required to — for example tax records relating to invoicing.

legalSections.title: Who we share it with
legalSections.body:
We share information only where it is necessary to deliver a project or to operate the business:

  • Project team and workshop. Designers, project managers, craftsmen and site supervisors need contact details and drawings to do the work.
  • Approved subcontractors and suppliers. Where a specialist trade is engaged, we share only what that trade needs — typically scope, location and contact for access.
  • Landlords, building management and authorities. Where approvals, permits or access permissions require a named applicant.
  • Professional advisers. Accountants and legal advisers, bound by confidentiality.
  • Service providers. Email delivery and website hosting, under written terms that prohibit use of your data for their own purposes.

We do not share personal information with advertisers or data brokers.

legalSections.title: Where it is stored
legalSections.body: Project records are stored on systems operated from Pakistan. Some service providers — for example email delivery and website hosting — may process information in other jurisdictions. Where that happens we rely on the provider's contractual commitments and, where applicable, standard data-transfer safeguards. Server logs are retained for a limited period and are not combined with your enquiry data.

legalSections.title: How long we keep it
legalSections.body: Enquiries that do not become projects are kept for twenty-four months, so we can recognise you if you return. Project records, contracts, drawings and correspondence are kept for ten years after handover, matching the workmanship warranty period. Invoicing and tax records are kept for the period required by Pakistani law. Journal subscriptions are kept until you unsubscribe, plus a short suppression record so we do not re-add you by mistake.

legalSections.title: Your rights
legalSections.body:
Subject to applicable law, you may ask us to:

  • Provide a copy of the personal information we hold about you.
  • Correct information that is inaccurate or incomplete.
  • Delete information, where we have no legal or contractual reason to keep it.
  • Restrict or object to particular processing.
  • Receive your information in a structured, machine-readable format.
  • Withdraw consent for the journal at any time.

Write to studio@woodexinterior.pk and we will respond within thirty days. Some rights are limited where records must be retained for warranty, contractual or tax reasons — if we cannot delete something we will explain why.

legalSections.title: Security
legalSections.body: Enquiry forms are transmitted over HTTPS. Access to project records is limited to the people who need them, and shared files are access-controlled. No system is perfectly secure, so we also keep manual verification for anything involving payment instructions or changes to bank details — we will never accept a change of payment details by email alone without a callback to a number already on file.

legalSections.title: Cookies and local storage
legalSections.body: This website uses the minimum storage needed to function. A small record in your browser's local storage remembers your chosen surface theme and text-density preference so the site looks the way you set it on your next visit. This is not used to identify you and is not shared with anyone. If analytics are enabled they use a short-lived session record to count page views without building a cross-site profile. You can block or delete cookies and local storage in your browser settings; the site remains usable if you do, but your display preferences will not persist.

legalSections.title: Children
legalSections.body: This website is aimed at adults commissioning interior design, fit-out and construction services. We do not knowingly collect information from children. If you believe a child has sent us information, contact us and we will delete it.

legalSections.title: Changes to this notice
legalSections.body: We update this notice when our practices, services or legal obligations change. The date at the top of this page shows the current version. Material changes will also be announced on the website rather than only in this document.

accessibility.legalIntro: We want this website to be usable by everyone, including people using assistive technology, keyboard-only navigation, screen magnification or a reduced-motion setting. This statement describes what we have done, what we are still doing, and how to tell us when something fails.

legalSections.title: Conformance target
legalSections.body: We target the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 level AA. We test against that standard during development and re-test when a section template changes materially. Conformance is a moving target on a living site, so we treat this statement as current rather than permanent.

legalSections.title: Measures we have taken
legalSections.body:
• Semantic structure. Every page has one h1 and a logical heading order; landmarks identify banner, navigation, main, complementary and contentinfo regions.
  • Keyboard operation. All navigation, accordions, sliders, tabs, filters, lightboxes and forms are reachable and operable by keyboard, with visible focus styling and logical focus order.
  • Focus management. Opening the mega menu or a lightbox moves focus into it and traps it there; closing returns focus to the control that opened it. Escape closes both.
  • Skip link. A skip-to-content link is the first focusable element on every page.
  • Text alternatives. Every content image carries a meaningful alt; purely decorative images and icon glyphs are hidden from assistive technology.
  • Contrast. Body text, headings, links, buttons and form labels meet a minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio against their background; large display text meets 3:1.
  • Resizable text. The layout holds together up to 400% zoom and reflows to a single column without horizontal scrolling.
  • Motion control. All animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion, marquee bands stop, and reveals become instant state changes rather than transitions.
  • Form usability. Every field has a persistent visible label, required fields are marked in text as well as by symbol, errors are announced and described in words, and validation does not depend on colour alone.
  • Structured data. Services, projects, articles, FAQs, organisation details and breadcrumbs are published as schema.org JSON-LD so assistive technology and search engines read the same content.
  • No autoplaying media. Video and audio never start automatically, and any media player exposes accessible controls.

legalSections.title: Display preferences
legalSections.body: The site offers surface themes and text-density settings that persist in your browser's local storage. These are an additional convenience, not a replacement for your own system or browser settings — font size, colours, contrast and reduced motion set at the operating-system level are always respected first.

legalSections.title: Known limitations
legalSections.body:
• Legacy pages. Older prototype pages retained at the repository root predate this system and have not been re-audited. The pages generated from the current templates are the accessible set.
  • Embedded maps. Office location maps are embedded from a third party whose player we do not control; each office card therefore also lists the full address in text and links to an external map.
  • Complex tables. The comparison and pricing tables are wide. They scroll horizontally on small screens, and we are working on a stacked card alternative for the narrowest viewports.
  • Drag interaction. Project carousels support dragging as a convenience, but every rail also has accessible previous and next controls and can be navigated by keyboard.
  • Photography. Some project photography contains small embedded text — signage, drawings, labels — that cannot be fully conveyed in an alt attribute. Case studies therefore repeat the key facts in the body text.

legalSections.title: How we test
legalSections.body: We test with current versions of Chrome, Firefox and Safari on desktop, and Chrome and Safari on mobile. We test keyboard-only navigation, screen-reader behaviour with NVDA and VoiceOver, zoom and reflow at 400%, forced-colours and high-contrast modes, and the reduced-motion setting. Every section template change is checked against these cases before it is published.

legalSections.body:
If you find something that blocks you, tell us — we would rather fix it than explain it. Include the page address, what you were trying to do, and the assistive technology or browser you were using.

legalSections.title: Formal complaints
legalSections.body: If you are not satisfied with our response you may raise the matter with the relevant consumer protection or disability rights authority in your jurisdiction. For users in Pakistan, the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority and the provincial consumer protection bodies both handle complaints about digital services.
